findings.title: Task 2.2's trail-location enumeration omits the archived-trail branch
findings.recommendation: Task 2.2 glosses trail-location resolution as "(change/explore/architecture)" while the orbit-emit-composition delta additionally specifies the project-scope location (covered at CLI level by task 3.1) and the archive emit's distinctive post-move resolution — scanning orbit/changes/archive/ for *-<name>/ matches, taking the lexically greatest, with the clean not-found error — which no engine or test task names (the group-2/3 test enumerations and the 9.3 smoke also skip the archive emit). The spec is unambiguous, so this is a coverage gloss rather than a fork risk, but extending 2.2's parenthetical to "(change/explore/architecture/archived/project)" and adding the archived-trail landing to a test bullet would close the gap the same way task 4.3 closed the orientation one.

commentary: Strict validation and 25/25 fingerprints green; zero @review: residue outside trail records; the scenario diff across all eleven modified capabilities shows no silent drops — the two apparent removals are the deliberate verify-first retirement and the 6-to-7 spine-field bump, and the architect sweep dedup leaves scenario sets byte-identical with the one normative home verified in baseline. The architecture-seam family closure from the latest walk held at every anchor I probed: dual-scope target resolution, the handoff mirror for both the architect emit and the architecture-clean review, the doc-scoped walk's confirm pointer, and the per-doc iteration ordinal all read as one voice now. The change remains conspicuously self-compliant — its own chunk preamble parses under the grammar it specifies, its explore.md carries the zero-entry open-questions case its counter must handle, and its design.md hosts the first authored Touchpoints instance in the entry grammar the checks parse. Engine citations (gates.ts :77/:397, the schema v3 phase ids, the R-d-8 sweep home) were spot-verified against source and held. The only residual softness is enumeration glosses in tasks.md relative to the fully-specified deltas — the archived-trail resolution being the one branch no task or test bullet names — which is a late-catch risk, not a fork risk.
